paper.title: Time-varying Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization with Experts: no-regret in logarithmically-many side queries

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandit optimization with expert side queries
unmapped: Each f_t lies in an RKHS with bounded kernel k(x,x) <= M_k^2 and ||f_t||_k <= B (B used in beta_t)
Per-round variation bounded: sup_x |f_{t+1}(x)-f_t(x)| <= 1 (not a total variation budget V_T)
Learner may additionally query an expert for noisy evaluations of the current f_t at O(log^d t) points per round
Regret is dynamic: against max_x f_t(x) at each round
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of sequentially optimizing a reward function $f: \Dset \times \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ where $\Dset \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a compact convex set... $y_t = f(x_t, t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T (\max_{x} f_t(x) - f_t(x_t))$

conditions: Assumption 1: f_t in RKHS with k(x,x) <= M_k^2 and ||f_t||_k <= B
expert queried O(log^d t) times per round with noisy updated observations
tuning: discard observations with injected variance > sigma^2 log t

source.label: Thm:regret
source.quote: Take any $0 < \delta \leq 1$ ... Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, by asking to an expert $\mathcal{O}\left(\log^d (t)\right)$ queries per time step, SparQ-GP-UCB attains a cumulative dynamic regret of $R_T = \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{ Td \log^{d+5}(T)}\sqrt{\log\left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right) +  d \log^{d+3}\left( d\log\left(T \right) \right)}\right) = \Ot(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Regret uses extra expert observations beyond bandit feedback. Horizon marked anytime since algorithm does not use T, though theorem says 'Let T be a time horizon'. Constants (sigma, B, M_k) hidden. Computational complexity theorem (O~(T^2)) not recorded as performance bound.
